programme_page_note: "Programa" is a same-page anchor (#clube-programa) on the homepage, not a separate URL. The homepage itself server-renders the full upcoming-events calendar via the EventON WordPress plugin.
central_feed_note: No central multi-event ICS/webcal subscription feed was found through the bounded first-party site investigation (the homepage HTML and its linked assets). The only "subscribe" mechanism present is an unrelated Mailchimp newsletter form. Each event exposes its own separate one-VEVENT .ics download instead. This records the result of that bounded investigation, not a claim that no such feed could exist anywhere on the site.

ics_discovery_mechanism.summary: Each event card in the homepage's EventON calendar renders a 'Calendário' link whose href is a first-party WordPress admin-ajax.php endpoint. The event's stable EventON post ID is also independently exposed as a data-event_id attribute on that event's container <div>, which is the recommended discovery point (not the ICS href's query string).
ics_discovery_mechanism.ics_link_evidence: Calendário
ics_discovery_mechanism.url_params_client_supplied_note: CONFIRMED BY DIRECT TEST (not assumed): the server does not re-validate sunix/eunix against its own stored event data. Re-requesting event_id=3794 with a deliberately wrong sunix/eunix (year 2099) returned an ICS whose DTSTART/DTEND echoed the wrong client-supplied values verbatim. This means the authoritative date/time for an event lives in the HTML page's rendered link (or the data-time attribute on the event container), not in the ICS endpoint itself — the ICS endpoint is a templating service, not a validating one.
ics_discovery_mechanism.also_present_but_unused_in_this_proof: Each event container also carries inline Schema.org Event HTML microdata (itemscope itemtype='http://schema.org/Event', itemprop='url'/'name'/'startDate'/'endDate'/'eventStatus'), plus a distinct stable permalink of the form https://hcp.pt/events/{slug}/ used for social-share links. Neither was investigated further in this bounded ICS proof; noted here as a discovery lead for a future task, not evidence of a JSON-LD acquisition path (this is inline microdata, not a <script type="application/ld+json"> block).

requests_made.purpose: confirm reachability before a full fetch
retrieve the programme page HTML to discover ICS links
diagnostic re-fetch of event 3794 with identical parameters, to test whether UID/DTSTAMP are stable across repeated downloads
requests_made.finding: UID and DTSTAMP both differed from the first fetch; all other fields (SUMMARY, LOCATION, DESCRIPTION, DTSTART, DTEND) were byte-identical. Not retained as a fixture — this response exists only to establish the UID-instability finding recorded below, not as sample event data.

requests_made.purpose: diagnostic fetch of event 3794 with deliberately incorrect sunix/eunix, to test whether the server trusts client-supplied timestamps
requests_made.finding: DTSTART/DTEND in the response echoed the deliberately wrong 2099 values verbatim, confirming the endpoint does not validate timing parameters against its own stored event data.

findings.uid_stability: NOT STABLE. Repeated downloads of the same event_id return a different UID and DTSTAMP each time (confirmed by direct re-fetch, request 12), while all substantive fields (SUMMARY, LOCATION, DESCRIPTION, DTSTART, DTEND) remain identical. The ICS UID must not be used as a stable source_record_id for this source.
findings.stable_identifier: The stable identifier is the EventON post ID, exposed as event_id in the discovery link's query string AND independently as a data-event_id="..." attribute on each event's container <div> in the programme page HTML. This event_id does not appear anywhere inside the ICS payload itself — it must be carried through from the HTML discovery step by any future collector, not recovered from the ICS text alone.
findings.line_endings: Mixed within every one of the 9 retained files: the first 2 lines (BEGIN:VCALENDAR, VERSION:2.0) are CRLF-terminated; all 10 remaining lines (from PRODID onward, including inside VEVENT) are LF-only. Identical pattern across all 9 fixtures, so this appears to be a stable quirk of this endpoint's output rather than per-request noise.
findings.line_folding: None observed. Every property, including a 343-character unescaped DESCRIPTION line, is emitted on a single unfolded line, exceeding the RFC 5545 75-octet folding recommendation without folding.
findings.escaping: Only backslash-escaped commas (\,) were observed (19 occurrences across the 9 fixtures, exclusively within DESCRIPTION values). No escaped semicolons (\;) and no escaped-newline sequences (\n or \N) were observed in any retained fixture.
findings.timezone_behaviour: All DTSTART/DTEND values use the UTC form (YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ). No TZID parameter and no bare local-time DTSTART/DTEND were observed anywhere in the 9 fixtures. DTSTAMP, however, is emitted WITHOUT a trailing Z or TZID (e.g. 20260823T182144) — inconsistent with RFC 5545 §3.8.7.2, which requires DTSTAMP always be expressed in UTC form. DTSTAMP's offset should be treated as unspecified/floating, not assumed to be UTC.
findings.fields_confirmed_absent: STATUS, ORGANIZER, URL, and any recurrence property (RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE) were absent from every one of the 9 retained VEVENT blocks. These were not invented or assumed present.
findings.all_day_dates: Not observed. All 9 sample events are timed events; no VALUE=DATE all-day DTSTART/DTEND was encountered.
